lines.text: Your autos trust the robot's pose, and every skid goes into it and stays there.
Odometry drifts further the longer you drive. A camera that sees a tag gives an answer that doesn't drift. It's noisy, but the error doesn't grow.
An AprilTag has an ID and a known spot on the field. From its four corners, the camera works backwards to where the robot must be.
Those sightings come now and then, and they're noisy, so they don't replace odometry. The next lesson blends the two.
Mount the camera where it sees the scoring tags while you're scoring, and give it its own breaker.
Never mount it level and square to a tag. Head on, small errors smear the answer. At an angle, the answer tightens up.
Try it. Move the camera until the cloud of answers is tight.
In the camera's web page, load the field map, pick the AprilTag pipeline, and turn the exposure down.
Enter where the camera sits on the robot, calibrate it with the ChArUco board, and give it a name.
Hold a tag a meter away. You should see its ID, the right distance, and a pose that holds steady.
Write down the camera's name. Next, the code feeds these sightings into the pose.
